mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% in a month coincides with a 20-day S&P 500 forward return positive as investors anticipate rate hikes and preemptively sell long-term equities.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3 in the current month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during pre-inflation spike periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly rise in PAYEMS exceeding 2,000 jobs signals strengthening labor market demand, which precedes a 5-day S&P 500 forward return positive as equities price in hiring strength.
failure_condition: Over 12 consecutive months with PAYEMS > 2000, 5-day forward returns are not consistently positive (average negative or flat).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in INDPRO above 1% for two months indicates weakening manufacturing capacity, which predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return negative as investors anticipate profit compression.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During INDPRO contraction phases, 20-day forward returns are not significantly below the mean of expansion periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in both HOUST (retail sales) and RSAFS (institutional demand) above their 12-month averages for three months signals robust aggregate demand, producing a 60-day S&P 500 forward return positive.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month avg and RSAFS > 12-month avg for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 100 such demand expansion windows, 60-day forward returns are not statistically superior to a neutral baseline (mean 0, t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 1% for 4 consecutive months, absent a coincident inflation spike, predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return negative as the Fed signals policy easing is complete and rates may hold.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% for four consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 0.2% in the same period
failure_condition: During such post-tightening periods, 20-day forward returns are not consistently negative across multiple non-overlapping windows (average flat or positive).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly UNRATE decline below 5% for two consecutive months suggests labor market softening, which precedes a 5-day S&P 500 forward return negative as investors reassess valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During UNRATE cooling phases, 5-day forward returns are not systematically negative (average non-negative).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time drop in GDPC1 (GDP) of at least 3% in the quarter preceding the decision date, not accompanied by a comparable drop in CPIAUCSL, predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return negative as profit expectations fall.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 3% in the prior quarter and CPIAUCSL falls < 1% in the same quarter
failure_condition: During such GDP-only shocks, 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than during comparable GDP-neutral periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A regime shift to a tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising > 0.25% month-over-month for two months) combined with a flat or declining HOUST series predicts a 60-day S&P 500 forward return negative as investors anticipate higher rates and muted demand.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 0.25% for two consecutive months AND HOUST <= previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: During such regime shifts, 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during equivalent pre-tightening windows (t-test p > 0.05).
